description: We are Team Penguins of Madagascar, a team passionate about technology, innovation, and space exploration. Our goal is to develop an innovative health-monitoring solution for astronauts during space missions. We are interested in software development, data analysis, AI, and user-friendly design. We welcome motivated members with skills in programming, healthcare, biomedical engineering, AI/ML, and design who want to contribute to this exciting challenge.
summary: ASTRA PULSE is an interactive health-monitoring and decision-support platform, not designed for diagnosis, platform, designed to help astronauts assess and manage their physical and psychological well-being during long-duration space missions. The system collects health indicators, including cardiovascular measurements, sleep, fatigue, respiratory rate, blood oxygen, motion sickness, and body temperature. Using a Python-based assessment engine informed by NASA research, it evaluates individual readings, compares them against mission-specific references and personal historical baselines, and identifies potentially concerning combinations of health indicators. Results are presented through an interactive dashboard with clear OK, WATCH and ACT statuses, explanations and recommended actions. Beyond monitoring, ASTRA PULSE provides guided wellness activities, including resistance training, breathing exercises and sleep-improvement practices adapted to different space environments. By combining research-informed assessment, personalized monitoring and preventive guidance, the project aims to strengthen astronaut autonomy, support early identification of health concerns and contribute to safer, healthier long-duration missions.
details:
We developed ASTRA PULSE, a personalized astronaut health-monitoring and decision-support system.

The central idea is that astronauts on long-duration missions cannot depend on continuous access to medical professionals. They need to recognize changes in their own health and understand when those changes require attention.

Our application collects multiple health indicators, including cardiovascular readings, sleep, fatigue, respiratory rate, blood oxygen, motion sickness and body temperature.

What makes ASTRA PULSE different is that it does not simply compare every astronaut against generic health ranges. It also establishes individual baselines and considers mission phases, historical changes and combinations of health indicators.

For example, if an astronaut experiences insufficient sleep alongside worsening reaction time, the system can identify this combined pattern and explain why it deserves attention.

We also integrated preventive wellness activities, so the astronaut is not just informed about a potential problem but is given practical guidance on maintaining their health.

We used NASA research and technical resources to inform our indicators and assessment rules, with clear distinctions between NASA-supported evidence and our own software-defined thresholds.

Our ultimate goal is to make health self-assessment more accessible, personalized and actionable for astronauts exploring beyond Earth.
